text:
Eli: FYI Riverstone wants a 1-week presales POC to move from CompetitorX -> Redwood. Focus: compat layer, prompt/response parity, function-call mapping, and embedding billing. Need quick plan.
Priya: Do we have their traffic profile? burstiness and avg seq lengths will change batching/latency guidance.
Eli: Notes from AE: mostly read-gen (spikes to ~180-220 RPS for short prompts), a handful of long-context flows (1-2 sessions at ~6k tokens), and heavy embedding volume (~50k small texts/day).
Mark: Main enterprise asks: SOC2 + pen test, KMS integration, and a clause in their contract about cache eviction windows and EU data residency. That pushes Private/Dedicated conversation.
Devon: Technical gotcha: CompetitorX streams partial json pieces via a custom header (X-comp-chunk). Customers parse on-the-fly. Our streaming uses standard chunked events; we should include a shim that emits the same header sequence and chunk boundaries for the POC.
Sales-Eng: Pricing Q: how to present embeddings? For many small texts recommend batching + TTL cache at edge. We can propose a volume-tier embed price and a 30-day cache TTL default with configurable TTL for enterprise.
Priya: Also run tokenizer parity: small token differences can shift monthly billing materially. Request a 2k-sample tokenizer test and token-count deltas.
Devon: I'll prototype a fn-call alias layer. Example mapping we use in presales (simple JSON map):
```json
{"get_price_v1": "get_price", "lookup_user_v2": "lookup_user"}
```
Devon: The shim will: normalize function_call.name -> aliases[name] || name, and forward args unchanged. Will also optionally preserve legacy metadata header X-legacy-fn for their router.
Maggie: Streaming test plan: 10 long sessions (mix of 3-6 sub-chunks each) to confirm chunk boundaries and reconnection behavior. We'll validate that their parser receives identical chunk sizes and header sequence.
Mark: For billing equivalence, build a billing-estimator: replay 7 days of sample traffic through tokenizers and our cost model. Show estimated monthly delta in dollars with conservative 95th percentile of tokenization differences.
Security: Riverstone expects completed vendor questionnaire within 48-72h, plus SOC2 report and recent external pen test summary. They also requested KMS + customer-managed keys for Private setups.
Sales-Eng: Recommend we present two options: 1) Hosted trial with aliasing+stream shim + blended embedding rate for POC, 2) Dedicated/private offering for full residency + KMS if they sign an MSA. Pricing delta shown side-by-side.
Priya: Load test: simulate 220 RPS sustained for 30m and 2x spike to 500 RPS for 1m. Measure 95/99 tail latencies, token throughput, and any queueing.
Eli: Any hard blockers? legal/residency or security SLA delays would push to Dedicated track.
Mark: Legal flagged cache-eviction SLA (they want deterministic eviction within 24h). Our hosted product needs explicit cache eviction controls or we'll need to propose Private with guaranteed delete ops.
Devon: I'll drop a sample curl for shim mode for their engs to run:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/compat/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $POC_TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Compat-Mode: competitorx" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-gen-2","prompt":"Summarize...","stream":true}'
```
Maggie: Action items / owners: - Devon: fn-call alias shim + stream header compatibility (48h). - Priya: tokenizer parity test & load test harness (48-72h). - Sales-Eng: draft blended embedding price and hosted vs dedicated comparison (48h). - Security: start vendor questionnaire + collect SOC2/pen test artifacts (48h). - Mark: draft note on cache-eviction contractual language and Private deployment lift (48h).
Eli: Let's not promise residency for hosted POC. Offer Hosted with strong delete options + Dedicated for residency/guarantees.
Priya: Starting sampler now, will post token-delta histogram in-thread.
Devon: Stubbing alias map and shim image, will attach logs after smoke.
Sales-Eng: I'll include an example billing worksheet and suggested discount tiers for embedding volume.
Security: Uploaded vendor questionnaire to Riverstone portal, awaiting their confirmation email.
Maggie: Thanks team. If anyone hits a showstopper, escalate to me immediately. :+1:
